question: Can the bounded-drift container stop constructing edit programs immediately when the canonical shared patch context first exceeds the frozen 8 MiB limit, without changing any accepted container byte or rejection semantics?
mechanism: Replace the eager programs=[encode_program(...)] list with the same canonical content-order loop, append each program in order, and raise the existing 'bounded-drift shared edit context exceeds decode-unit limit' error immediately when len(patch)+len(program.raw) would exceed MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES. Accepted rows execute every same program in the same order and serialize the same entries/patch bytes; rejected rows can stop after the first irreversible context overflow.
exactness_argument: MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES is a hard decoded-context representation limit; patch length is monotone under canonical program concatenation.

Once cumulative patch bytes plus the just-built next canonical program exceed MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES, no remaining member can reduce the patch; the historical implementation must reject the same candidate after constructing all programs.
For every accepted candidate, no early condition fires, so program order, program bytes, offsets, entry metadata, compressed contexts and final physical bytes remain unchanged.
The error class and rejection message remain unchanged for shared-context overflow.
decision: ADVANCE_EXACT_FAILFAST_IMPLEMENTATION. This is a zero-byte accepted-path execution improvement with material losing-family work elimination on exact hostile sources. It is not the Shifted/Boundary create-frontier mechanism, but it lowers bounded-drift carrying cost and prevents rejected shared-context candidates from paying provably useless remaining edit construction.
kill_or_narrow: any rejected candidate changes error class/reason or becomes accepted
